benchmarks.title: Unpolarized Transverse Momentum Distributions from a global fit of Drell-Yan and Semi-Inclusive Deep-Inelastic Scattering data
benchmarks.cut_summary: Q > 1.4 GeV; 0.2 < z < 0.7; |P_hT| < min[min(0.2 Q, 0.5 z Q) + 0.3 GeV, z Q]; HERMES vector-meson-subtracted zxpt-3D tables and the COMPASS vector-boson-subtracted release; published W^2 and lepton-y cuts retained
benchmarks.use: external count and cut-definition benchmark; reproduce independently before comparing fit quality
benchmarks.caveat: The published 1547 is not a raw-table total and cannot be used as an unexplained normalization target. Point-level selection, duplicated projections, vector-meson subtraction, and error treatment must be reconstructed from the paper and source tables. The paper's HERMES zxpt-3D supplemental archive and covariance sidecars are not yet mirrored here, so a literal 344-row HERMES reproduction remains pending.

benchmarks.title: Flavor dependence of unpolarized quark Transverse Momentum Distributions from a global fit
benchmarks.reported_sidis_scope: updated HERMES/COMPASS unpolarized SIDIS within a global N3LL fit
benchmarks.reported_fit_quality: chi2/Ndat = 1.08 for the combined DY+SIDIS analysis
benchmarks.dataset_relation_to_2206_07598: The paper states that its experimental dataset is identical to the MAPTMD22 analysis, including the 1,547-point HERMES/COMPASS SIDIS scope.

sidis_selection.pht_cut: |P_hT| < min[min(0.2 Q, 0.5 z Q)+0.3 GeV, z Q]

benchmarks.sidis_normalization_note: The N3LL analysis applies a kinematics-dependent normalization factor to the SIDIS prediction, constructed from a collinear SIDIS numerator through O(alpha_s^2) divided by the integrated W-term denominator; this is a theory/formalism component that must be implemented and validated explicitly.
benchmarks.use: formalism, dataset-selection, and flavor-dependent TMDFF benchmark
benchmarks.caveat: This is a literature comparison, not a source of raw rows. Its exact point count, cuts, normalization factors, and covariance conventions must be recorded from the paper before reproducing any result. The 2022 analysis reports SIDIS-specific normalization factors for higher-order corrections; these are a formalism benchmark, not an instruction to rescale our data silently.

benchmark_policy: Use the 1547-point result as a reproducibility checkpoint for the clean HERMES/COMPASS stage, then add other global families progressively. Do not pad or force a fit to reach 1547 by counting incompatible diagnostic observables.
